question: Slovakia has recently adopted legislation intended to transpose the Pay Transparency Directive1. Concerns have been raised about the compatibility of several provisions of the national legislation with the directive.

These relate to the exclusion of certain categories of senior public officials and statutory office holders from the legislation’s scope, the postponement of workers’ access to pay information rights beyond the transposition deadline, and the transposition of criteria for assessing work of equal value.
These provisions may limit the protection provided by the directive and affect its uniform application across the EU. 1.

Does the Commission consider the exclusion of state servants holding public office, statutory office holders, and other senior public-sector officials appointed by the Slovak Parliament, President or Government or members of the Slovak Government from the scope of the national legislation to be compatible with Article 2 of the directive?

Does the Commission consider it compatible with Article 4(4) of the directive to replace the concepts of ‘skills’ and ‘effort’ with narrower national definitions, and to reduce the requirement that relevant soft skills ‘shall not be undervalued’ to merely taking them into account?

Does the Commission consider the postponement of workers’ access to pay information rights beyond 7 June 2026 to be compatible with Articles 7 and 34, given that the directive does not appear to provide for such a transitional period?

Directive (EU) 2023/970 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 10 May 2023 to strengthen the application of the principle of equal pay for equal work or work of equal value between men and women through pay transparency and enforcement mechanisms (OJ L 132, 17.5.2023, p. 21, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2023/970/oj). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.8.2026) In line with the Better Regulation framework1, the Commission assesses transposition in two stages: a completeness check to verify that all necessary national measures have been notified; and a conformity check to assess whether those measures fully comply with the Directive. The Commission is currently examining Member States’ notifications.
Where a Member State fails to transpose the Directive by the deadline, the Commission may initiate infringement proceedings under Article 258 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

As regards the substance of national implementing measures, including the Slovak legal provisions referred to by the Honourable Member, the Commission will, in accordance with established procedures, carry out a detailed assessment of their compliance with the Directive, as part of its conformity review of all implementing measures in all Member States, thereby helping to ensure consistent implementation across the EU.
Such assessment will take place once the transposition review is completed, as it requires a comprehensive examination of relevant national labour, civil and procedural law provisions.
